name: Sound Localization
definition: The ability to tell the direction from which a sound originated.

benchmarks_mapped.name: DCASE2020 Task 3 (Sound Event Localization and Detection)
DCASE2020 Challenge Task 3 (Sound Event Localization and Detection)
DCASE2025 Task 3 (Stereo SELD in Regular Video Content, Track A audio-only)

benchmark.name: DCASE2020 Task 3 (Sound Event Localization and Detection)
benchmark.model_or_system: USTC-iFlytek system (Du_USTC, ranked #1 team in DCASE2020 Task 3)
benchmark.human_reference: General adult population with normal hearing. Everyone uses sound localization; in work settings this means people who orient to sound sources in noisy or reverberant environments.

benchmark.name: DCASE2020 Challenge Task 3 (Sound Event Localization and Detection)
benchmark.model_or_system: USTC'20 (USTC team, ResNet-Conformer ensemble with four-stage data augmentation; top-ranked DCASE2020 Task 3 system)
benchmark.metric: Location-dependent F-score F≤20° (%), on the DCASE2020 Task 3 evaluation set
benchmark.human_reference: General adult population with normal hearing, the typical person who judges sound direction in everyday and work settings. This comparison assumes a hypothetical listener hearing the scenes binaurally.

benchmark.name: STARSS22
benchmark.metric: degrees (LE_CD, class-dependent localization error; lower is better)

benchmark.name: LOCATA
benchmark.metric: mean azimuth error, degrees (lower is better)
benchmark.human_reference: General adult population with normal hearing. Sound localization is a basic perceptual ability used in everyday and workplace settings, not a trained specialist skill.

benchmark.name: DCASE2023 Task 3
benchmark.metric: location-dependent F-score F≤20° (%, macro, segment-based) on the STARSS23 evaluation set
benchmark.human_reference: General adult population with normal hearing. Sound localization is a basic perceptual ability used in everyday and work settings (e.g., locating a speaker, alarm or vehicle), not a specialist skill.

benchmark.name: DCASE2025 Task 3 (Stereo SELD in Regular Video Content, Track A audio-only)
benchmark.human_reference: General adult population with normal hearing. Sound localization is a basic perceptual ability used across many jobs, such as driving, safety monitoring and audio work.

benchmark.name: DCASE2026 Challenge Task 3
benchmark.model_or_system: SAID (Semantic Acoustic Imaging Detector, PaSST variant) - top-ranked Track A team submission
benchmark.metric: Macro-averaged Mask mAP (IoU 0.50:0.95), in percent, on the official DCASE2026 Task 3 Track A evaluation set
benchmark.human_reference: General adult population with normal hearing, listening to the scenes (for example, binaurally rendered spatial audio). Sound localization is a basic perceptual ability, not a specialist skill.
